biggest_catch: Only ~20% of applicants are accepted — and it's designed for healthcare students, not general caregivers.
catches: Official pages: only ~20% of caregiver applicants are accepted after background checks and interviews.
Built for pre-health/nursing/medical students — not a general caregiving marketplace.
Non-medical care only; many personal-care tasks (bathing, injections, wound care) are excluded.
Earnings depend on family bookings in your area — nothing guaranteed.

c1.evidence: CareYaya's official pages (careyaya.org) state: 'Cost to Family: ~$15–$18 per hour (flat rate, no contracts)... Families pay caregivers directly, platform is free to use.' Caregivers are vetted students providing companionship and daily-activity help to seniors — a live, provider-owned deal channel.

c2.evidence: Official: families pay caregivers directly at ~$15-$18/hour; rates vary by booking — variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: apply as a caregiver, pass the background check and interview, complete training, accept family care requests.

c4.evidence: Official: 'platform is free to use' — families pay caregivers directly; no fee charged to caregivers.

eligibility: Pre-health, nursing, and healthcare students able to pass background checks and interviews (about 20% acceptance).
notes: Scenario: senior caregiving by students. CareYaya pairs healthcare students with families needing non-medical senior care (companionship, mobility, meals, light housekeeping, pet care). Families pay caregivers directly at ~$15-$18/hour; the platform is free to use. Highly selective (~20% acceptance). Variable, never guaranteed.
